0|5cb431dcf8048572e9ffc6c30cdbd8832cbe502d|torvalds~linux|/home/usuario01/Titan-Files-Research/src/_00/output/C/torvalds~linux|False|"ibmvnic: Return error code on TX scrq flush fail
In ibmvnic_xmit() if ibmvnic_tx_scrq_flush() returns H_CLOSED then
it will inform upper level networking functions to disable tx
queues. H_CLOSED signals that the connection with the vnic server is
down and a transport event is expected to recover the device.
Previously
column2: ibmvnic_tx_scrq_flush() was hard-coded to return success.

column1: Therefore
column2: the queues would remain active until ibmvnic_cleanup() is

column1: called within do_reset().
The problem is that do_reset() depends on the RTNL lock. If several
ibmvnic devices are resetting then there can be a long wait time until
the last device can grab the lock. During this time the tx/rx queues
still appear active to upper level functions.
FYI
column2: we do make a call to netif_carrier_off() outside the RTNL lock but

column1: its calls to dev_deactivate() are also dependent on the RTNL lock.
As a result
column2: large amounts of retransmissions were observed in a short

column1: period of time
column2: eventually leading to ETIMEOUT. This was specifically

column1: seen with HNV devices
column2: likely because of even more RTNL dependencies.

column1: Therefore
column2: ensure the return code of ibmvnic_tx_scrq_flush() is

column1: propagated to the xmit function to allow for an earlier (and lock-less)
response to a transport event.
